Another offers dozens of features but takes too long to set up. A third looks simple at first, then needs paid upgrades the moment you want timelines, automation, or better reporting. Trello is the better choice if you want a simple visual workflow and nothing more.

articles.title: What the Knox warranty void flag actually means after you flash Samsung firmware
articles.excerpt: If you have ever flashed a Samsung phone, you have probably heard someone warn you about Knox. The warning usually sounds dramatic: trip Knox and your warranty is gone forever. Like most warnings in t…
articles.body: If you have ever flashed a Samsung phone, you have probably heard someone warn you about Knox. The warning usually sounds dramatic: trip Knox and your warranty is gone forever. Like most warnings in the flashing world, that one has a real core and a lot of exaggeration around it. Here is what the flag actually is, what it changes, and what it does not. What Knox actually is Knox is Samsung's security platform, built into the phone at a hardware level. It creates a protected area on the device where sensitive things live: work profiles, payment data, biometric templates, and encryption keys. Apps that need real security, like Samsung Pay and Secure Folder, trust that protected area. If something tampers with the phone's software at a low level, Knox is designed to notice.

articles.title: Why a Static PPTX Is Often the Right Format for Sharing Your HTML Presentation
articles.excerpt: When people convert an HTML presentation to PowerPoint, they often assume the goal is a fully editable file. Sometimes it is. But in my experience, most of the time the person asking for "the PowerPoi…
articles.body: When people convert an HTML presentation to PowerPoint, they often assume the goal is a fully editable file. Sometimes it is. But in my experience, most of the time the person asking for "the PowerPoint" just wants to open it, present it, or forward it. For those cases, a static PPTX, where each slide faithfully reproduces what you designed, is not a compromise. It is often the better choice. What "static" means here A static PPTX keeps the visual result of each slide intact, typically as a high-resolution image placed on a standard PowerPoint slide. You can open it in PowerPoint, Keynote or Google Slides, reorder slides, add speaker notes, and present it full screen.

articles.title: JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC? A Plain-English Guide to Choosing Image Formats
articles.excerpt: You take a photo on your phone, try to upload it to a website, and get an error: "unsupported format." Or you save a screenshot and the text looks fuzzy. Or a simple logo somehow takes up five megabyt…
articles.body: You take a photo on your phone, try to upload it to a website, and get an error: "unsupported format." Or you save a screenshot and the text looks fuzzy. Or a simple logo somehow takes up five megabytes. Image formats cause a surprising amount of everyday frustration, but the basics fit on one page. Here is a plain-English guide to the formats you are most likely to meet. JPG: the all-rounder for photos JPG, also written JPEG, is the most widely supported image format in the world. It uses lossy compression, meaning it throws away detail the eye is unlikely to notice in order to make files smaller. That works brilliantly for photographs, with their smooth gradients and natural textures.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.title: Medusa's eye, Halloween fireballs and more: 5 skywatching targets to look out for this spooky season
articles.excerpt: Five spooky skywatching targets perfect for naked eye stargazing this Halloween!
articles.body: The spooky season is officially here! To celebrate, we've put together a list of five Halloween-themed skywatching targets that you can enjoy with nothing but the naked eye or binoculars and, of course, clear skies. Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects. Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites. The Pleiades open star cluster Don't be fooled by their beauty; the blue-white stars of the Pleiades are dripping in spooky lore.
articles.author: Anthony Wood

Rosetta’s Selfie Explanation: This Rosetta spacecraft selfie was snapped on October 7th, 2014. At the time the comet-chasing spacecraft was about 472 million kilometers from planet Earth, but only 16 kilometers from the surface of comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko . Looming beyond the spacecraft near the top of the frame, dust and gas stream away from the comet’s curious double-lobed nucleus .
